overview: A one-page Department of State list of papers filed under “Cotton Manufacture in Japan.” It indexes two numbered items: an Osaka report reviewing Japan’s cotton situation, prepared at the suggestion of Agricultural Attaché Owen L. Dawson in Shanghai, and a telegram from Argentina reporting Japanese press coverage of a proposed reorganization of Japan’s cotton-spinning industry and the transfer of equipment to the Philippines. The underlying reports are not included on this page.

subfiles.title: List of papers on cotton manufacture in Japan
subfiles.about: An index records an Osaka review of Japan’s cotton situation and an Argentina telegram concerning the proposed reorganization of Japanese cotton spinning and transfer of equipment to the Philippines.
subfiles.summary: The sheet lists two papers under the subject “Cotton Manufacture in Japan.” Item 13 is an Osaka report, associated with Allison and dated August 17, reviewing the Japanese cotton situation and outlook at the suggestion of Agricultural Attaché Owen L. Dawson in Shanghai. Item 14 is Argentina telegram no. 8390, associated with Reed and dated January 28, reporting Japanese press information about reorganizing Japan’s cotton-spinning industry and transferring equipment to the Philippines. No years are supplied for the indexed items, and the printed “10/12/45” appears to be the revision date of Form DS-46 rather than the date of this particular list.

interest: Although only an index sheet, this document identifies two potentially valuable records and concisely preserves their subjects, provenance, and filing sequence. It links Japanese cotton-industry planning to American agricultural reporting in Shanghai and to proposals for transferring Japanese spinning equipment to the Philippines. It is particularly useful as a finding aid for reconstructing missing or separately filed reports and for tracing postwar concern with the redistribution and reorganization of Japanese industrial capacity.
